title: Tom Varley reckons the powder for his own shafts
summary: In the last week of an Cèitean, with the road below Cnoc thais already cut, Tom Varley and Angus Rennie's cousin work out by lamplight how much powder will bring the lower galleries down clean and how much less would only crack the timbering.

title: A shepherd's path left unwatched
summary: The regiment below Cnoc thais spends the better part of a month digging and drilling before it finds a shepherd's path along the northern ridge too steep for anything but goats, which the town's own watchers had judged not worth the watching.

title: Tom Varley fires his own two shafts
summary: Tom Varley goes down each shaft alone in the grey hour and fires the charges himself, refusing another man's offer to do it, and stands at the shaft-head afterward watching the smoke come up thin against a low sky.

title: Forty-one taken at Cnoc thais
summary: The regiment's muster gives forty-one holdouts marched south as prisoners from Cnoc thais; it gives no figure for those already gone up into the hills by paths the shepherd had not shown the soldiers.

title: Tom Varley takes the rabbit path
summary: Tom Varley leaves the falling town by a path he last walked as a boy after rabbits, with five other hewers who choose, each in his own time, to take it rather than stand and be taken.

title: A warning at the shielings
summary: On the second night out, sitting at a small fire among the summer shielings, one of Tom Varley's party argues that the near hills will not be let stand a season longer, and the others find no better guess to set against him.

title: Seven parties on the windy coast
summary: Word passes between separate handfuls out of Cnoc thais, the last of Muileann àrsaidh's scattered folk and one party out of Àth naomh, until seven parties in all, somewhat short of two hundred souls, sit on the same stretch of unclaimed ground.

title: The officer's report names them of no shire
summary: A patrol officer halted at the boundary stone of Seann Vell writes into his report that the ground beyond lies outside any shire the Board's writ runs in, and reaches, for the seven parties sitting on it, the name that the open record keeps thereafter.

title: Cairstine's coast path
summary: A trader named Cairstine, who has walked the coast path with salt and needles twice a year since before the war had a name, carries the season's word up to the fisherfolk and the seven parties both.

title: The second fleet's raising told on the windy coast
summary: Cairstine tells Tom Varley's fire that the second fleet was raised that season at the southern Seann Skell out of the harbour towns and the Rite's own boatmen, to hold water that had stood quiet a generation.

title: The burned boat's crew put ashore
summary: The crew of the salt-boat burned off Àth bheag are put ashore some days after at the light of Baile ìseal, with nothing left of a season's work but the clothes they stand up in.

title: A fisherman's word on the door left open
summary: A fisherman of Baile ìseal tells Cairstine that a kingdom which shuts a door on nothing much will find another door, one it did not think to watch, standing open behind it, and she carries the saying north with the rest of the season's news.

title: Tom Varley's private tally
summary: Through the autumn Tom Varley keeps, unwritten, a tally in his own head of the men who came out of Cnoc thais with him, the men the regiment marched south, and a field left unploughed below Àth leathan he cannot yet set down as finished.

title: The first evening at the edge of the sea
summary: In the last clear evening before the hard weather turns, Tom Varley stands on a strand of black shingle at the edge of the windy coast and watches the light go out of the sky without any sunset to mark the day's end.

title: Mary Kessock's two ends
summary: At the council of Cnoc thais in the chapel room an old widow, Mary Kessock, says a town threatened by soldiers it cannot fight may be taken whole or leave the takers nothing and go. The room begins to make ready to leave.

title: Mary Kessock stays at her door
summary: When Cnoc thais falls, the old widow Mary Kessock stays at her own door and raises a hand to Tom Varley as he goes up the rabbit path.

title: A hind brought down on the windy coast
summary: On the walk to the windy coast a man of Àth naomh brings down a hind with a single cast of the spear he had carried from his own town.

title: Calum Odhar's byre
summary: A widower of the windy coast, Calum Odhar, who fishes a two-man boat out of a cove with no name, gives the byre behind his house to the six men of Cnoc thais and asks only whether they can mend a net.
